lines.trans: Mateo... Clara... please tell me room six is free tonight.
No, Ernesto, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.
Every key from one to seven is occupied, and room eight has wet paint.
What a disaster! Yesterday I wrote down a phone booking on the tablet without my glasses!
Wait a moment, let me look at the tablet screen and the notebook together.
Let me guess. Did you promise somebody a room we do not have?
Ernesto! Room seven is already occupied and you booked a second guest into seven!
And he arrives here at eight o'clock this evening—in forty minutes!
I told you that tablet is a trap.

Wait... what is on the third floor, at the top of the stairs?
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Está libre = it is vacant / available.

examples.trans: It is a free piece.
is free

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Always feminine even when referring to two people.

examples.trans: The couple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las parejas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the couples from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Al sur = to the south.

examples.text: El sur es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The south is very important here.
We talk about the south.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.
We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Describes a busy person or an occupied room/table.

examples.trans: It is a busy piece.

examples.text: Todas las llaves de la uno a la siete están ocupadas, y la ocho tiene pintura fresca.
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is occupied, and room eight has wet paint.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.
The guesthouse has eight rooms.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: La pintura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The paint is very important here.
We talk about the paint.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.trans: It is a cool piece.

examples.text: Bien. Pon estas hierbas frescas por encima antes de servirlos.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh herbs on top before serving them.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: ¡Qué desastre! = What a disaster!

examples.trans: The disaster is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desastres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the disasters from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with preterite tense.

examples.trans: Yesterday we fixed the boiler.

examples.text: Llegué a Valencia ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I arrived in Valencia yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.
Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Tener una reserva = to have a booking.

examples.trans: The reservation is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reservas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reservations from the door.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

meanings.note: Electronic tablet or chocolate bar.

examples.trans: The tablet is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tabletas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tablets from the door.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.
He left home without a coat.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?
He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Computer or phone screen.

examples.trans: The screen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las pantallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screens from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.trans: Sit next to the window.
We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: Can you guess who called today?
She guessed the answer right away.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Lo prometo = I promise.

examples.text: Te prometo volver antes de las siete.
examples.trans: I promise you I will return before seven.
They promised to visit us next week.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: I will be back in forty minutes.

examples.text: Son las seis y cuarenta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is six forty-five.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.
What is your name?

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Tiene trampa = there is a trick/catch to it.

examples.trans: The trick is here.

examples.text: Vemos las trampas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tricks from the door.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Impersonal stem-changing verb (o -> ue: llueve).

examples.trans: Today it is raining heavily in Valencia.
Last night it rained until ten.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Plural los hoteles.

examples.trans: The hotel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hoteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hotels from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of vacío (empty).

examples.trans: It is a full piece.

examples.text: Vaya... ¿con esta lluvia? Todos los hoteles cerca de la estación parecían llenos.
examples.trans: Oh dear... in this rain? Every hotel near the station looked full.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.trans: It is a third piece.
Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Top-floor room with sloping roof beams.

examples.trans: The attic room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las buhardillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attic rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: It is a sunny piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.
Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.
